checks: J1 a new window journal starts empty at revision 1 and reopens identically with the same transport
J2 a window is signed, verified and made durable in ONE commit, with one debit of N fee ceilings
J3 nothing new can be prepared while any attempt is pending
J4 a chunk window must be non-empty, distinct, in range and at most MAX_WINDOW
J5 a tampered or malformed pending list is refused when the journal is reopened
J6 resolveMany resolves only the listed attempts, in one commit, and refuses everything else
J7 an expiry needs BOTH the missing-signature proof and a height past the blockhash lifetime; one unproven entry refuses the whole call
J8 a ticket serves only its own kind, only once, and only at the revision it was prepared
J9 the attempt counter counts every signed attempt, window or single
R1 a window is charged N fee CEILINGS
R2 a shrinking pending list takes no debit, and a debit on a resolution is refused
R3 attempts can only enter an EMPTY list and a retained attempt can never be replaced or duplicated
R4 the per-request funding cap bounds the CUMULATIVE cost of windows; a refused window stores and charges nothing
R5 the attempt cap counts the whole window, and a window that fits exactly is accepted
R6 the quote refuses a window when ANY fee is unavailable or above the cap, or the balance cannot cover all of it
R7 settlement journals keep the original single-attempt funding rules in the v2 repository
R8 record sizes: a window record up to 512 KiB, every other record stays at 32 KiB, foreign labels are refused
R10 the window quote is bound to the sponsor, to a non-empty bounded list and to the exact sum
R9 a window and its debit become durable together or not at all, across SIGKILL of the process
S1 a whole chunk phase with window 128: every chunk once, one commit to sign and one to resolve each window, the buffer equals the wire
S2 window 1 is the original sender: one attempt, one commit pair and one transaction per chunk
S3 the step results of a clean window are pending, then step_confirmed; a lost send is not a failure
S4 a restart after the durable commit but before any send releases exactly the stored bytes and signs nothing new
S5 a partial landing resends ONLY the chunks the cluster has not seen, with the same bytes
S6 a blockhash that expired with the chunk still unknown resolves it as EXPIRED with proof, and the chunk goes into a fresh window
S7 a chunk that shows up at the second lookup is CONFIRMED, never expired
S8 a chunk that lands with an error is recorded as failed, the others are resolved, and the step does not go on silently
S9 a confirmed status whose effect is not visible in the buffer stays pending as awaiting_progress
S10 a failing commit releases nothing: no send, no pending, no debit
S11 a simulation that rejects any chunk stops the window before anything is signed
S12 a window left pending is finished whatever window the restarted sender is configured with, and later windows obey the new size
S13 the window size is validated by the sender and never exceeded
S14 only one step runs at a time
S15 a cluster that has not reached the minimum slot is a pending result, not a failure
S16 a status that is only processed is neither a confirmation, nor an expiry, nor a reason to send again
S17 an attempt that shows up as processed only between the two lookups is not sent again with a dead blockhash
S18 the sender refuses an RPC that answers inconsistently: another signature, a short status list, a pending list that changed before the resend
A1 the adapter checks the request id on every call and refuses to bind a payment that is no longer settling
A2 opening the task wires the v2 journal and v2 funding, validates the window before reserving funds, and reopens identically
A3
C1 cleanup closes the receipt FIRST and the buffer second, each once, and the sponsor gets both rents back
C2 nothing is ever closed while the payment is still being published
C3 the buffer is closed only while it still holds exactly the proof we hold
C4 an unsealed or incomplete buffer is never closed
C5 the close instructions are exactly the verifier's and the buffer program's, on the request's own accounts, signed by the sponsor alone
C6 only the two request accounts can be named: no other target, no extra field
C7 a restart between the two closes does not close the first again, and finishes the second
C8 a restart after the durable commit but before the send releases exactly the stored bytes
C9 a close that lands with an error is recorded as failed, the account stays, and retries are bounded by the attempt cap
C10 an uncertain send outcome keeps the same signed attempt and never signs another
C11 a close whose blockhash expired before it landed is resolved as expired with proof, and signed again
C12 a close counts as done only when the account is really gone, not when the status says so
C13 each close costs one fee ceiling, and the per-request cap bounds the cleanup like everything else
C14 once everything is closed a fresh sender finds nothing to do and sends nothing
C15 a missing receipt does not stop the buffer from being closed, and a missing buffer does not stop the receipt
C16 the withdrawal kind is cleaned the same way
C17 the task validates the cleanup option before reserving any funds, and defaults to cleaning
C19 a stored close whose descriptor is not canonical
cluster: model (harness.mjs): real buffer layout and rules, real SQLite, real Ed25519 signing, real transaction decoder, a verifier receipt and the two close opcodes as modelled from the programs' source; no validator, no verifier program, no pool
proves_nothing_about: the deployed programs closing accounts as modelled
